notes: The motor shield is stacked on the Due by its header pins. The Due's digital and analog pins are single group ports in the catalogue ('D0-D53' and 'A0-A11'), and each can be used only once. So the shield has matching group ports ('D0-D13' and 'A0-A5'), and each stacks onto the Due with one joined+electrical pair.
The sketch uses pins 3 (PWM_A), 9 (BRAKE_A), 12 (DIR_A) and A0 (SNS_A). All of them pass through those group connections. GND, VIN and 5V are stacked individually.

The motor's two wires are permanently attached, so there are no separate jumper-wire parts. Motor port 1 (red wire) goes to channel A+ and port 2 (black wire) goes to A-. The motor is symmetric, so the polarity only sets the spin direction.

The wall wart (12V in the example) plugs into the Due's DC jack. The shield draws motor power from the Due's VIN pin. The validator rejected a 'lead' port on a socket, so the wall wart's barrel plug uses kind 'ball'. That is the only listed kind that pairs with a socket and stands in for a barrel plug in a jack.
The USB cable to the computer is visible in the photo and is needed to upload the sketch. The usb-cable catalogue entry has no ports, so those edges use null ports on the cable side.
The wheel on the motor is not a listed part and is left out.
